mainEntity.name: Does the Renault Kadjar 1.2 TCe have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.2 TCe (H5F400, H5F402) uses a timing chain, not a belt. The chain is prone to premature wear, particularly on early examples. Symptoms include rattling noises on cold start, which can indicate the chain is stretching. If left unaddressed, the chain can snap, causing catastrophic engine damage. Timing chain - not a belt. Known weak point on the 1.2 TCe. Rattle on cold start is a warning sign. Oil changes every 6,000-8,000 miles are recommended for longevity.

mainEntity.name: Is the Renault Kadjar 1.3 TCe more reliable than the 1.2 TCe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the 1.3 TCe (H5Ht) is generally considered more reliable than the 1.2 TCe. Developed jointly with Daimler, it features improved engineering and doesn't suffer from the same widespread timing chain issues. However, some owners have reported oil leaks from the rocker cover seal and turbo-related noises. 1.3 TCe: More modern design, fewer timing chain issues. 1.2 TCe: Known timing chain weakness. 1.3 TCe: Watch for oil leaks and turbo noises.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Kadjar 1.2 / 1.3 TCe - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Renault Kadjar launched in 2015 as the brand's compact crossover SUV, built on the Renault-Nissan CMF-CD platform shared with the Nissan Qashqai. The petrol range initially featured the 1.2 TCe four-cylinder turbo engine, before being replaced by the more modern 1.3 TCe developed jointly with Daimler for the 2019 facelift.

milestones.description: Kadjar launches with 1.2 TCe (H5F) petrol, 130hp, four-cylinder turbo
H5F402 revised engine code introduced with emissions updates
Facelift (Phase 2) introduces 1.3 TCe (H5Ht) petrol, developed with Daimler, available in 140hp and 160hp outputs
Kadjar production ends, replaced by Renault Austral

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every petrol engine fitted to the Renault Kadjar - from the early 1.2 TCe H5F to the modern 1.3 TCe H5Ht - is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Renault Kadjar 1.2 / 1.3 TCe Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Kadjar TCe petrol engines are broadly capable units, but several failure patterns have emerged. **Timing chain wear on the 1.2 TCe** is the most significant problem, while the **1.3 TCe** suffers from oil leaks and turbo-related issues. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Wear - Why the Renault Kadjar 1.2 TCe Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The 1.2 TCe engine suffers from premature timing chain wear. The problem manifests as rattling noises during cold starts and can lead to the chain snapping, causing catastrophic engine damage. Renault's recommended oil change intervals of up to 20,000 km (12,000 miles) are believed to contribute to chain stretch.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full timing chain kit including tensioner and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if chain is stretched - prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of damaged valves and cylinder head work
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has snapped and caused valve damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, full engine replacement with upgraded timing components
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution if chain failure has caused extensive damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Kadjar 1.2 TCe (2015-2018) is worth approximately £3,000-£10,000 `[THIRD-PARTY]`. Timing chain replacement (£700-£1,200 specialist) is a significant but worthwhile investment for most examples. For vehicles under £3,000, carefully evaluate whether a full engine replacement makes sense.
problems.recommendation: The 1.2 TCe's timing chain is the critical weak point. If you hear a rattle on cold start, have the chain inspected immediately - catching it early can prevent a £1,200 repair becoming a £4,000+ engine replacement. Use high-quality oil and change it more frequently than Renault's official recommendation (every 6,000-8,000 miles is advisable).

problems.h4: Oil Leak - Why the Renault Kadjar 1.3 TCe Loses Oil from the Rocker Cover
problems.rootCause: The 1.3 TCe engine can develop oil leaks from the rocker cover valve seal line along the top of the engine, between the fuel injector rail and the spark plug rail. This is a known issue reported by owners across multiple Renault and Mercedes applications that share this engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the rocker cover gasket and seal
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early - stops the oil leak
Only if oil loss has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Rocker cover gasket replacement (£200-£350 specialist) is a minor expense relative to the value of any Kadjar 1.3 TCe.
problems.recommendation: If you notice oil spots on your driveway or a burning oil smell, have the rocker cover seal inspected. This is a straightforward repair that should not escalate to engine replacement if addressed promptly.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Noise and Failure - Why the Renault Kadjar 1.3 TCe Hisses and Rattles
problems.rootCause: Some 1.3 TCe owners report hissing noises under load and metallic rattle sounds on cold start. The hissing is often attributed to the turbocharger or air intake system. While not always catastrophic, these symptoms can indicate developing turbocharger issues.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full diagnostic check of turbo and intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Identifies the root cause of noise
Only if turbo failure has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Turbo repairs (£800-£1,500 specialist) are a significant but justifiable expense for a Kadjar worth £5,000+.
problems.recommendation: If your 1.3 TCe is making unusual noises, don't ignore them. Have the turbocharger inspected by a specialist. Early diagnosis can prevent a relatively simple repair from becoming a full engine replacement.
